_about: Lessons from our live practice games (notes/agent_changelog.md, datasets/runs/). Retrieved into the model's prompt by case type. Evidence = session ids.
general: Suppliers react to the STRUCTURE of the term sheet (contract length, lead time, payment days) far more than to arguments; P07's price path was identical across 6 games and 5 agent versions.
Never push after final_offer: one extra ask made the P07 supplier walk away (c5d845883158676c). Accept, or send back its own prose alternative verbatim (P10 agreed, 2d91214cf7693eff).
Never cite an index that rose, even framed as 'below your ask': it answered 'Your figures confirm our case: that driver rose' (P07 0f754b1368387b8e, P10 675fc6b9c1c8c291).
Answer its questions with checkable data: it asked 'Which volume can you commit to?' 3x until we stated it (P07); forecasts (fc:) were 'verified and taken into account'.
Unverifiable claims invite more questions: 'around 5 times our current business' got 'please provide the exact figures behind' 3x (P07 d67da0a2d2360134).
Don't ask for strain we don't need: a lead time faster than our need was 'technically unfeasible' and priced at a premium (P10).

Suppliers state their cost shares in the opening ('X rose N% … and is M% of our cost'): a calculation from their own shares is the data they ask for (P02 da8d0e3d77ce091c: 'without additional verified data to substantiate your target price, our flexibility remains highly restricted').
Data disarms data-naive owners ('we did not know that - a fair point', P01 e3e0b7be271e9371); elsewhere it usually 'holds, but does not change our calculation'.
Each data ID counts once per case; re-citing reads as padding ('we received a lot of material').
Keep the e-mail in English and never promise a lever that is not negotiable in the case.
price_increase: P01 (stabilise, family foundry, data-naive owner): index data + short-notice argument + later effective date + faster payment → 0.85 in 3 rounds.
P02 (stabilise, group, pricing committee): it accepted 90-day payment but priced the financing (~6.7%/yr); final in round 4 at €372.15; wanted verified data behind our target.
bundling: P07: 24-month contract was the big win (+0.48); the kit-level calculation at its own prices got its best price (€5.40 @ 30 d); its final always lands at ~€5.49 @ 90 d in round 4; 36 months was priced higher.
capacity: P10 (secure_supply, allocation, approval ladder): goes final in ROUND 1 every time (5/5), so the first offer is everything; lead time below its own costs ~0.49% of price per day; its floor €31.90 @ 56 d (24 or 36 m alike).
renewal: P04 (routine, Neel's games): final in round 3; 90-day payment and a small price step scored 0.86.
rfq: Cite only rival offers that are cheaper than the bidder's own price; never show the leader worse prices.
quality: Ask for the 8D report and a binding ppm commitment within the must-have; cash-short suppliers react badly to heavy chargebacks.
raw_material: Hedged suppliers ('covered at fixed prices until …') answer market-index arguments with 'not our reality'; index clauses cost us when the path is positive.
